summary: Order failures began at 11:00 UTC, the same minute config change cfg-broker-timeout-ms lowered BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS on broker-gateway from 3000 to 800. broker-gateway err_rate went from 0.005 to 0.203, then 0.225. Its logs show requests aborted for exceeding the 800ms timeout. order-router, web-app and orchestrator then log HTTP 503s from broker-gateway, and order-router err_rate rose from 0.004 to 0.156 and then 0.174. order-router calls broker-gateway with weight 0.8, so its errors are downstream effects. The mean broker latency (about 217ms) is well below 800ms, so the failing requests must be a slow tail. I have no latency percentiles to confirm this, and I have not ruled out an independent broker-side slowdown. No other deploy near onset fits the failure pattern.

hypotheses.statement: Lowering BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS from 3000 to 800 on broker-gateway made it abort slower broker requests that used to succeed. These surface as 503s to order-router, orchestrator and web-app and cause order failures and timeouts.
hypotheses.label: high

hypotheses.statement: The broker upstream has a slow latency tail (the earlier 'responded slowly' warnings) that was harmless at the 3000ms timeout and is now exposed. This is a latent condition, not a new fault.

unresolved: The share of broker requests slower than 800ms is not measured, because no percentile latency data was available.
The error log query was truncated (198 matches, 50 returned), so the full error mix after 11:05 was not reviewed.
Whether aborted broker requests were still executed on the broker side, and so whether any orders are in an inconsistent state, is unknown.
The mean latency drop after 11:00 is only an inference (e10).
An independent broker-side slowdown is not ruled out.

actions.text: Roll back BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS on broker-gateway to 3000 (revert cfg-broker-timeout-ms), or set a value justified by broker p99 latency.
actions.rationale: The change coincides with onset and the errors are explicit aborts at the 800ms limit. Reverting should restore the pre-11:00 error rate of about 0.005.

actions.text: After the rollback, confirm that broker-gateway and order-router err_rate return to about 0.005 and 0.004. Then check that no orders were left in an ambiguous state after aborted broker calls.
actions.rationale: This verifies the cause. Aborted requests may have been executed by the broker anyway, so confirmation is needed.

actions.text: Collect broker-gateway latency percentiles (p95, p99) and the slow-request warning rate to choose a safe timeout. Add a review gate and canary for timeout config changes.
actions.rationale: Only mean latency is available, so the size of the slow tail is unknown.
